reasons: The outcome objective passes Augur: reviewer-upheld tier moves per unit are an outcome, and spending or activity is not the goal. The declared 1 lane, 29 orders and 6,000,000 units fit STAGE_CAPS[0]. All required supervisor fields are positive, and their non-enforcement by Relay is disclosed.

All six acknowledged_findings answers are plan-specific. At least three concrete pre-mortem guards are implemented: filtered reviewer inputs, planted controls, bounded evidence prompts, census-versus-reviewed-tier reporting, and scoring missing results or reviews as no move. However, several stronger enforcement statements remain false.

A concrete budget bypass remains: --token-cap 0 passes wave.verify because it only rejects values greater than the approved budget. Probe and stage0 then set the engine cap to zero, and Engine._claim treats zero as disabling budget enforcement. This permits overshoot unrelated to the disclosed reservation excess.

Persisted state is still not validated before execution. wave.verify checks DRAW.json, but not STATE.json caps, progress, full_started or database jobs. Calling stage0 on a directory containing an interrupted full run passes verification with min(requested_cap, 6,000,000), while Probe uses the unmodified requested cap when full_started is true and resumes those full-run jobs before stage0 returns 'already done'. With the default arguments, a stage-0 invocation can therefore execute full-run work under a 10,000,000-unit ceiling.

The disclosed overshoot bound does not cover missing usage. Failed or timed-out turns can consume more than their recorded estimate, after which the engine continues admitting work and wait() can retry the failed step. Unrecorded excess can accumulate across successive turns, rather than being limited to the final in-flight turn per lane. An abrupt host crash can also lose a turn's usage entirely: reservations are in memory, and restart does not charge or reconcile the interrupted attempt. The owner's post-stage-0 stop condition cannot prevent overspending during stage 0.

First-pass artifacts are not protected. Engine._run requires the expected artifact but also accepts additional artifacts, and consumers select the latest artifact by name. A producer can supply an extra review.json that survives a failed reviewer step; a reviewer can replace result.json; and a repair turn can replace both result.json and review.json. Thus an unreviewed result can be scored as reviewed, and a ledger-informed reviewer or repair can change what is reported as the producer's first-pass conclusion. The plan's independence and first-pass immutability claims are false.

Several stated controls are defaults or different algorithms. Claude's $2 and 40-turn settings can be overridden by environment variables; --turn-timeout can exceed 900; Codex medium reasoning is not set unless supplied through configuration or the environment. Reservations ignore measured failed turns and ignore even successful measured maxima until three successful measured turns exist, contrary to 'largest turn yet measured'.

The provenance statements overstate the implementation. common.input_hashes covers the named finding-aid files, not the held text files workers read. Changing a held text after drawing does not trigger refusal. Slices are built at launch from the supplied checkout, not at draw time from a verified main checkout. The adapters retain usage and final artifacts, not an exhaustive record of every file and URL read.

For the normal supplied paths, model tools and pipeline storage provide no direct mechanism to file claims or alter repository statuses or counts. Probe rejects an internal data directory, and the report destination is owner-authorized. Repository writes are not a rejection ground here.
risks_noted: The owner-directed Bentham exception and pending review binding are accepted. Augur's zero forecast for an absent action must not be interpreted as measured zero cost or yield.

Blind initial prompts omit explicit ledger status, cell labels and machine tiers, while retaining finding-aid leads. Reviewer blindness is accurately described as instruction-only. A reviewer that reads the ledger can pass it to the repair producer through review.json; repaired conclusions can therefore be contaminated. That is tolerable only when the first-pass artifacts remain protected and repairs remain separate.

The census starting tier, sparse planted controls, shared finding-aid evidence, unreviewed repair results and adaptive Wilson-interval stopping limit measurement interpretation. These disclosed or measurement-quality weaknesses are not independent rejection grounds.

The directing session's stop conditions are operational controls, not automatic checks. The supplied telemetry does not itself establish an exhaustive audit of whether a producer accessed a denied source.

reasons: The outcome objective passes. The declared 3 lanes, 235 cumulative genuine orders and 10,000,000 cumulative units fit STAGE_CAPS[1], which permits 3 lanes, 300 orders and 40,000,000 units. The six lesson responses are specific, and at least three implemented pre-mortem guards exist. The owner-authorized Bentham and configuration-ramp exceptions are accepted in principle.

The full-run gate now checks a minimum measured-order count, estimated turns and the fitted projection before raising the cap. However, Probe.__init__ calls _resume_unfinished before full() performs any gate. A full invocation against an interrupted, unfinished stage 0 can therefore resume work with three workers before discovering that stage0_done is false. This violates the stated sequencing of the owner-authorized ramp.

Runtime state remains outside the reviewed-plan validation. wave.verify bounds DRAW.json caps, whereas _picks uses STATE.json caps and progress; it does not validate existing jobs against the reviewed frame and cumulative order limit. full_started also bypasses the projection gate without a persisted binding to the approved configuration. Zero caps are accepted, and a resumed full run with --token-cap 0 can execute unfinished work with budget enforcement disabled before admission or projection logic stops it.

There is a concrete parallel reservation race. _advance_pipeline makes a job queued before the current worker's finally block removes active[job_id] and reserved[job_id]. Another worker can claim the next step of that same job and replace those entries. The previous worker then deletes the new step's reservation and cancellation handle. Subsequent work can be admitted while that turn is unreserved. The total can consequently exceed the cap even when every turn costs no more than its nominal reservation, which is beyond the disclosed overshoot.

Missing usage and crash recovery also invalidate the overshoot bound. Estimates can undercharge completed failed turns while additional turns launch, and an abrupt crash can leave a paid attempt without any usage record. A clean stage-0 estimate count does not protect against these failures during stage 1.

Artifact ownership is not enforced. Extra review.json or result.json artifacts from the producer, reviewer or repair step can replace the canonical records used by outcome() and report.analyse(). This defeats the promised independent review and preservation of first-pass blind conclusions, including when a reviewer reads the ledger despite its instructions.

The same inaccurate enforcement and provenance statements apply as in stage 0: provider ceilings and timeout are overrideable, medium reasoning is not forced, reservations do not immediately use every measured maximum, held texts are not hashed, slices are constructed at launch from the selected checkout, and read paths and URLs are not exhaustively logged.

No direct unauthorized repository-write path is established for normal execution with the supplied inputs. The model restrictions, external data directory and owner-directed report folder address that part of the launch requirements.
risks_noted: The owner's ramp exception is not inherently unsafe, but it is unsafe with work resuming before its gate and with the reservation race unresolved.

The projection is a forecast, not a completion guarantee. It includes terminal error-job costs, omits the future completion cost of already-drawn CAP-stopped orders, and falls back to pooled costs for sparse cells. These can make it optimistic even after cells shrink.

Reviewer blindness remains instruction-only, and unrestricted review feedback can disclose the ledger to repair producers. Finding-aid overlap also means first-pass agreement is not proof of independent correctness.
The owner must separately apply the failure-rate, informative-control, denied-read and remaining-40-orders conditions. full() does not implement those checks.

Adaptive stopping, budget-driven sample reduction, census-based starting tiers and unreviewed repairs require cautious interpretation. They are measurement risks rather than independent rejection grounds.

required_changes: Reject nonpositive unit caps before constructing Probe, and make Engine reject an invalid cap rather than treating zero as unlimited for this probe. Validate the effective cap actually passed to the engine, including on resume.

Validate persisted run state and database jobs against the reviewed draw, stage, cumulative order allowance and budget before workers can execute. Bind persisted state to the reviewed configuration. Refuse stage0 on full-run state, and move full-run eligibility and projection checks ahead of _resume_unfinished so an unapproved transition cannot resume work with three lanes.

Fix the parallel reservation lifecycle: prevent a queued next step from being claimed while its predecessor still owns the job's active entry, or use unique attempt identifiers and atomically release the predecessor's reservation before publishing the next step. A worker must never remove another attempt's reservation or cancellation handle.

Stop further admission and automatic retry when a turn's usage is unknown, unless its usage has been reconciled or conservatively bounded. Persist enough attempt information before launching a provider to detect interrupted, unaccounted attempts after a crash; refuse further execution until those attempts are reconciled. This must preserve the disclosed bound to the last in-flight turns rather than accumulating hidden excess.

Require each pipeline step to emit exactly its expected artifact, rejecting extra or duplicate artifact names. Select scoring artifacts by their authorized producer/reviewer step and actor, so later steps cannot replace first-pass results or supply their own independent review.

Make the declared provider controls effective: enforce Claude ceilings of at most $2 and 40 turns, reject timeouts above 900 seconds, and explicitly set Codex medium reasoning. Change reservation calculation to include the largest measured turn immediately, including measured failed turns, or revise the plans to describe the actual reservation algorithm and configurable defaults accurately.

Correct the provenance wording to state that the named finding-aid inputs are hashed, slices are built at launch from the selected checkout, and artifacts record cited sources rather than every read. Alternatively, implement the stronger claimed behavior by pinning all local evidence inputs, verifying the intended checkout, and retaining complete source-access telemetry. Explicitly identify repair feedback as a possible ledger-disclosure route while preserving immutable first-pass scoring.
